facts.text: Gramercy Park was founded in 1885 for religious instruction in the parish of the Epiphany and has survived as a landmark through generations.
The National Academy of Design and the Players Club, founded in 1888 by Edwin Booth, gave the square its artistic and intellectual gravitas.
A statue of Edwin Booth stands at the center of Gramercy Park, erected in 1918 to honor the famed Shakespearean actor.
The Gramercy Park Hotel opened in 1925 as a red‑brick bastion of old‑world charm that later hosted artists, musicians, and dignitaries.
Two keys are allocated to each original lot around the park; owners may buy a key for $350, with a $1,000 fee for a lost key.
The Players Club, located on the opposite side of the park, became a gathering place for actors, playwrights, and intellectuals including Mark Twain and John Barrymore.
